name: search_posts
title: Search X posts (currently unavailable)
description: Search public X (Twitter) posts (tweets) by keywords, #hashtags or X search operators such as from:jack. Currently unavailable: the upstream search backend is disabled, so calls fail fast with code "feature_unavailable" and retrying does not help. Instead, use get_profile_statuses for posts by a known account (from:jack -> {"handle":"jack"}) or get_post for a known post URL or ID. When search works it returns {posts:[...],returned,has_more,next_cursor?} with the get_profile_statuses post fields, at most count per call; pass next_cursor back unchanged as cursor for more.

q.description: Search query in X search syntax, 1-500 characters: keywords, "exact phrase", #hashtag, or operators such as from:jack. Example: "from:nasa artemis".

feed.description: "latest" (default) for the newest matching posts, or "top" for popular ones.

count.description: Maximum number of posts to return, 1-100 (default 10). Each call reads one upstream page (about 20 posts), so fewer can come back; has_more and next_cursor say whether to continue.

cursor.description: Omit for the newest results. To continue, pass next_cursor from the previous result of this tool exactly as returned, with the same q and feed.

response_format.description: "concise" (default): the compact fields listed in the tool description. "detailed": the full upstream objects, several times larger, so fewer fit in one result; use it only when you need a field that concise omits.

name: get_post
title: Get X post
description: Get one public X (Twitter) post (tweet) by URL or numeric ID: full text, author, time, engagement metrics, media, quoted post, reply target, link card, poll, Community Note, and the text of an X Article. Use it whenever you have a post link (x.com or twitter.com .../status/<id>) or ID, to read the full text of a list item marked text_truncated, or to open the post a reply answers (reply_to.post_id). Example: {"id":"https://x.com/jack/status/20"} or {"id":"20"}. Returns {post:{id,url,created_at,author{handle,name,verified?},text,lang?,metrics{replies,reposts,quotes,likes,bookmarks?,views?},reply_to?{handle,post_id},quote?,media?,card?,poll?,article?,community_note?}}; optional fields appear only when present, and response_format "detailed" returns the upstream post object instead. Unknown or deleted posts return code "not_found"; posts that are not public return "restricted". Replies to a post and whole threads cannot be listed.

id.description: The post: its numeric ID as a string, e.g. "20", or its URL, e.g. "https://x.com/jack/status/20" (twitter.com and mobile links work; /photo/1 suffixes and ?query strings are ignored). Quote numeric IDs: JSON numbers above 2^53 lose precision.

response_format.description: "concise" (default): the compact fields listed in the tool description. "detailed": the full upstream objects, several times larger, so fewer fit in one result; use it only when you need a field that concise omits.

name: get_profile
title: Get X profile
description: Get the public profile of one X (Twitter) account by handle or profile URL: display name, bio, location, website, join date, follower, following and post counts, verification and protected status. Use it to check that an account exists or to describe it; for its posts use get_profile_statuses. Example: {"handle":"nasa"} ("@nasa" and "https://x.com/nasa" also work; case-insensitive). include_about=true adds X's "About this account" data (the country the account is based in, username changes). Returns {user:{handle,name,id,url,description?,location?,website?,joined,followers,following,posts,likes,media_count,verified?,verified_type?,protected?,about?}}. Unknown accounts return code "not_found" and suspended accounts "restricted"; numeric account IDs are not supported.

handle.description: The account: a handle with or without "@", e.g. "nasa" or "@nasa", or a profile URL such as "https://x.com/nasa" (case-insensitive). A post URL also works; its account is used. Numeric account IDs are not supported.

include_about.description: true adds about: X's "About this account" data (based_in country, whether that is accurate, how the account was created, username changes) when X provides it. Default false.

response_format.description: "concise" (default): the compact fields listed in the tool description. "detailed": the full upstream objects, several times larger, so fewer fit in one result; use it only when you need a field that concise omits.

name: get_profile_statuses
title: Get profile posts
description: Get recent public posts (tweets) and reposts from one X (Twitter) account, newest first; include_replies=true also returns its replies. Use it for "what did @user post" questions and for from:<user> requests; for one known post use get_post. Example: {"handle":"nasa","count":5}. Returns {posts:[...],returned,has_more,next_cursor?,note?}; posts have the get_post fields, but text over 1,000 characters is cut (text_truncated:true; get_post returns all of it). A post with reposted_by is a repost: author is the original poster and created_at the original time, so the list is not strictly sorted by created_at. Each call reads one upstream page (about 20 posts) and returns at most count of them (default 10); while has_more is true, pass next_cursor back unchanged as cursor for older posts. Protected, suspended and unknown accounts return code "restricted" or "not_found".

handle.description: The account: a handle with or without "@", e.g. "nasa" or "@nasa", or a profile URL such as "https://x.com/nasa" (case-insensitive). A post URL also works; its account is used. Numeric account IDs are not supported.

count.description: Maximum number of posts to return, 1-100 (default 10). Each call reads one upstream page (about 20 posts), so fewer can come back; has_more and next_cursor say whether to continue.

cursor.description: Omit for the newest results. To continue, pass next_cursor from the previous result of this tool exactly as returned, with the same handle and include_replies value.

include_replies.description: true also returns the account's replies, each with reply_to. Default false. A cursor only works with the include_replies value it was issued for.

response_format.description: "concise" (default): the compact fields listed in the tool description. "detailed": the full upstream objects, several times larger, so fewer fit in one result; use it only when you need a field that concise omits.

name: get_profile_media
title: Get profile media posts
description: Get recent public posts with photos or videos from one X (Twitter) account, newest first. Use it to find an account's images or videos; for all of its posts use get_profile_statuses. Example: {"handle":"nasa","count":5}. Returns {posts:[...],returned,has_more,next_cursor?} with the get_profile_statuses post fields; each media item is {type:"photo"|"video"|"gif",url,alt?,thumbnail_url?,duration_s?}, where url is the original image or the video file. Upstream pages vary in size, so a call can return fewer than count posts; while has_more is true, pass next_cursor back unchanged as cursor for older media.

handle.description: The account: a handle with or without "@", e.g. "nasa" or "@nasa", or a profile URL such as "https://x.com/nasa" (case-insensitive). A post URL also works; its account is used. Numeric account IDs are not supported.

count.description: Maximum number of media posts to return, 1-100 (default 10). Each call reads one upstream page, which varies in size, so fewer can come back; has_more and next_cursor say whether to continue.

cursor.description: Omit for the newest results. To continue, pass next_cursor from the previous result of this tool exactly as returned, with the same handle.

response_format.description: "concise" (default): the compact fields listed in the tool description. "detailed": the full upstream objects, several times larger, so fewer fit in one result; use it only when you need a field that concise omits.

name: get_trends
title: Get X trends
description: Get the current trending topics on X (Twitter), each with a context label such as "Sports · Trending". The region is chosen upstream and cannot be set, and this tool does not return posts about a trend. Example: {"count":10}. Returns {trends:[{name,context?,rank?}],returned,note?}; an empty list means the upstream has no trends right now and is not an error. count is 1-100 (default 10); values above 50 are reduced to 50, the upstream maximum.

count.description: Maximum number of trends to return, 1-100 (default 10). Values above 50 are reduced to 50, the upstream maximum.

name: typeahead
title: X typeahead (currently unavailable)
description: Get X (Twitter) search-box suggestions (accounts and topics) for a partial name. Currently unavailable: the upstream search backend is disabled, so calls fail fast with code "feature_unavailable" and retrying does not help. If you know or can guess the handle, call get_profile instead. When it works it returns {users:[{handle,name,verified?,followers}],topics:[...]}, at most count of each (default 10).

q.description: Partial account name, handle or topic to complete, 1-200 characters. Example: "nasa".

count.description: Maximum number of suggestions of each kind (accounts and topics), 1-100 (default 10).

name: get_openapi
title: Upstream capability summary (deprecated)
description: Deprecated and kept only so existing callers keep working; it will be removed in a future version. Returns a short static summary of the upstream endpoint behind each tool and whether it is currently advertised as available; it no longer returns the upstream OpenAPI document. You do not need it for X lookups, because tools/list already describes every tool. Example: {}.

name: get_profile_articles
title: Get profile Articles
description: Get X Articles (long-form posts) published by one X (Twitter) account, newest first. Use it to find an account's Articles, then call get_post with a result's url to read the full Article text. Example: {"handle":"jack","count":5}. Returns {posts:[...],returned,has_more,next_cursor?,note?} with the get_profile_statuses post fields plus article{title,preview_text}. While has_more is true, pass next_cursor back unchanged as cursor for older Articles.

name: get_profile_followers
title: Get profile followers

Use it for "who follows @user" questions; for the account itself use get_profile. Example: {"handle":"nasa","count":20}.
